final_template:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: 'Serverless Step Functions workflow that publishes custom events to a custom Amazon EventBridge event bus, plus an EventBridge rule that forwards every event on that bus to a CloudWatch Logs log group for testing and debugging. The template is self-contained and creates the event bus, log group, log resource policy, IAM role, rule and state machine that it references.'

Parameters:
  Environment:
    Type: String
    Description: Environment name used for tagging and included in the published event detail.
    Default: dev
    AllowedValues:
      - dev
      - test
      - prod
    ConstraintDescription: Value must be one of dev, test or prod.

  LogRetentionDays:
    Type: Number
    Description: Number of days that debug events are retained in the CloudWatch Logs log group.
    Default: 14
    AllowedValues:
      - 1
      - 3
      - 5
      - 7
      - 14
      - 30
      - 60
      - 90
      - 120
      - 150
      - 180
      - 365
      - 400
      - 545
      - 731
      - 1096
      - 1827
      - 2192
      - 2557
      - 2922
      - 3288
      - 3653
    ConstraintDescription: Must be a retention period supported by CloudWatch Logs.

Resources:

  CustomEventBus:
    Type: AWS::Events::EventBus
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-custom-bus'
      Tags:
        - Key: Project
          Value: !Ref AWS::StackName
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref Environment

  EventDebugLogGroup:
    Type: AWS::Logs::LogGroup
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      LogGroupName: !Sub '/aws/events/${AWS::StackName}-debug'
      RetentionInDays: !Ref LogRetentionDays
      Tags:
        - Key: Project
          Value: !Ref AWS::StackName
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref Environment

  EventDebugLogGroupPolicy:
    Type: AWS::Logs::ResourcePolicy
    Properties:
      PolicyName: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-eventbridge-logs-policy'
      PolicyDocument: !Sub |
        {
          "Version": "2012-10-17",
          "Statement": [
            {
              "Sid": "AllowEventBridgeToWriteToDebugLogGroup",
              "Effect": "Allow",
              "Principal": {
                "Service": "events.amazonaws.com"
              },
              "Action": [
                "logs:CreateLogStream",
                "logs:PutLogEvents"
              ],
              "Resource": "${EventDebugLogGroup.Arn}:*"
            }
          ]
        }

  ForwardAllEventsRule:
    Type: AWS::Events::Rule
    Properties:
      Description: Forwards every event published to the custom event bus to the debug CloudWatch Logs log group.
      EventBusName: !Ref CustomEventBus
      EventPattern: {}
      State: ENABLED
      Targets:
        - Id: DebugCloudWatchLogsTarget
          Arn: !GetAtt EventDebugLogGroup.Arn
      Tags:
        - Key: Project
          Value: !Ref AWS::StackName
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref Environment

  StateMachineExecutionRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      Description: Execution role assumed by the Step Functions state machine to publish events to the custom event bus.
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: AllowStepFunctionsToAssumeRole
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: states.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: PutEventsOnCustomBus
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Sid: AllowPutEventsOnCustomEventBus
                Effect: Allow
                Action: events:PutEvents
                Resource: !GetAtt CustomEventBus.Arn
      Tags:
        - Key: Project
          Value: !Ref AWS::StackName
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref Environment

  PublishEventStateMachine:
    Type: AWS::StepFunctions::StateMachine
    Properties:
      StateMachineType: STANDARD
      RoleArn: !GetAtt StateMachineExecutionRole.Arn
      DefinitionString: !Sub |
        {
          "Comment": "Publishes a custom event to the custom EventBridge event bus created in this stack.",
          "StartAt": "PublishCustomEvent",
          "States": {
            "PublishCustomEvent": {
              "Type": "Task",
              "Resource": "arn:aws:states:::events:putEvents",
              "Parameters": {
                "Entries": [
                  {
                    "Source": "custom.stepfunctions.workflow",
                    "DetailType": "CustomWorkflowEvent",
                    "Detail": "{\"environment\":\"${Environment}\",\"message\":\"Custom event published by Step Functions\"}",
                    "EventBusName": "${CustomEventBus}"
                  }
                ]
              },
              "End": true
            }
          }
        }
      Tags:
        - Key: Project
          Value: !Ref AWS::StackName
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref Environment

Outputs:
  EventBusName:
    Description: Name of the custom EventBridge event bus.
    Value: !Ref CustomEventBus
  EventBusArn:
    Description: ARN of the custom EventBridge event bus.
    Value: !GetAtt CustomEventBus.Arn
  DebugLogGroupName:
    Description: Name of the CloudWatch Logs log group that receives all events published to the custom bus.
    Value: !Ref EventDebugLogGroup
  ForwardAllEventsRuleArn:
    Description: ARN of the EventBridge rule that forwards all events to CloudWatch Logs.
    Value: !GetAtt ForwardAllEventsRule.Arn
  StateMachineArn:
    Description: ARN of the Step Functions state machine that publishes events to the custom bus.
    Value: !Ref PublishEventStateMachine

final_template:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'

Description: >-
  AWS Cloud WAN global network and core network for centralized outbound traffic
  inspection across multiple AWS Regions. The core network deploys edge locations
  in us-east-1 and us-west-2, defines "production" (attachments isolated from one
  another) and "development" segments, an "inspection" network function group,
  tag-based attachment policies keyed on a "domain" tag, and segment actions that
  send all production and development traffic through the inspection network
  function group. VPC attachments are NOT created by this template; attachments
  are created by other stacks or tools and MUST be tagged with the key "domain"
  and one of the values inspection, production, or development so that the
  attachment policies below associate each attachment with the inspection network
  function group or with the matching segment.

Parameters:

  ProjectName:
    Type: String
    Default: cloudwan-inspection
    MinLength: 1
    MaxLength: 40
    AllowedPattern: '^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9-]*$'
    ConstraintDescription: >-
      Must start with a letter or digit and contain only letters, digits, and
      hyphens.
    Description: Name of the project that owns the Cloud WAN global and core networks.

  Environment:
    Type: String
    Default: production
    AllowedValues:
      - production
      - staging
      - development
      - test
    Description: Environment name used for cost allocation and ownership tagging.

Resources:

  GlobalNetwork:
    Type: AWS::NetworkManager::GlobalNetwork
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      Description: global network for centralized outbound traffic inspection
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${ProjectName}-global-network'
        - Key: Project
          Value: !Ref ProjectName
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref Environment

  CoreNetwork:
    Type: AWS::NetworkManager::CoreNetwork
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      GlobalNetworkId: !Ref GlobalNetwork
      Description: !Sub '${ProjectName} core network for centralized outbound traffic inspection'
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${ProjectName}-core-network'
        - Key: Project
          Value: !Ref ProjectName
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref Environment
      PolicyDocument:
        version: '2021.12'
        core-network-configuration:
          asn-ranges:
            - '64512-64555'
          inside-cidr-blocks:
            - '100.64.0.0/10'
          edge-locations:
            - location: us-east-1
              asn: 64512
            - location: us-west-2
              asn: 64513
        segments:
          - name: production
            description: >-
              Production workloads. Attachments are accepted automatically but
              are isolated from other attachments in the same segment.
            require-attachment-acceptance: false
            isolate-attachments: true
          - name: development
            description: >-
              Development workloads. Attachments are accepted automatically and
              use the default non-isolated attachment behaviour.
            require-attachment-acceptance: false
        network-function-groups:
          - name: inspection
            require-attachment-acceptance: false
        attachment-policies:
          # NOTE: The exact key used inside `action` to target a network function group
          # must be verified against the current AWS::NetworkManager::CoreNetworkPolicy
          # schema before deploying. `network-function-group` is the documented key; if
          # the schema in use differs, correct or omit this property rather than guessing.
          - rule-number: 100
            description: >-
              Attachments tagged domain=inspection are associated with the
              inspection network function group.
            condition-logic: or
            conditions:
              - type: tag-value
                operator: equals
                key: domain
                value: inspection
            action:
              association-method: constant
              network-function-group: inspection
          - rule-number: 200
            description: >-
              Attachments tagged domain=production are associated with the
              production segment.
            condition-logic: or
            conditions:
              - type: tag-value
                operator: equals
                key: domain
                value: production
            action:
              association-method: constant
              segment: production
          - rule-number: 300
            description: >-
              Attachments tagged domain=development are associated with the
              development segment.
            condition-logic: or
            conditions:
              - type: tag-value
                operator: equals
                key: domain
                value: development
            action:
              association-method: constant
              segment: development
        segment-actions:
          - action: send-via
            segment: production
            via:
              network-function-groups:
                - inspection
          - action: send-via
            segment: development
            via:
              network-function-groups:
                - inspection

Outputs:

  GlobalNetworkId:
    Description: The ID of the Cloud WAN global network.
    Value: !Ref GlobalNetwork

  CoreNetworkId:
    Description: The ID of the Cloud WAN core network.
    Value: !Ref CoreNetwork

  CoreNetworkArn:
    Description: The ARN of the Cloud WAN core network.
    Value: !GetAtt CoreNetwork.CoreNetworkArn

  CoreNetworkState:
    Description: >-
      The current state of the Cloud WAN core network. The core network policy is
      defined inline on the CoreNetwork resource, so no separate policy version
      attribute exists to expose; the resource state is surfaced instead.
    Value: !GetAtt CoreNetwork.State

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'

Description: >-
  Test resource for validating a template approval workflow. Deploys a
  CloudFormation WaitConditionHandle signaling endpoint carrying
  approval-workflow metadata and an SSM parameter stored under
  /iidy/template-approval/test/ that records the stack identity, a custom
  message, and whether the approval workflow is enabled. Fully self-contained:
  no external infrastructure is referenced.

Parameters:

  Name:
    Type: String
    Default: World
    Description: >-
      Subject of the greeting. Used in the WaitConditionHandle metadata and in
      the /iidy/template-approval/test/<Name> SSM parameter name.
    MinLength: 1
    MaxLength: 64
    AllowedPattern: '[A-Za-z0-9._-]+'
    ConstraintDescription: >-
      Must be 1-64 characters containing only letters, numbers, periods,
      underscores, or hyphens.

  CustomMessage:
    Type: String
    Default: Hello from CloudFormation
    Description: Custom message embedded in the SSM parameter value.
    MinLength: 1
    MaxLength: 256

  ApprovalWorkflowEnabled:
    Type: String
    Default: 'true'
    AllowedValues:
      - 'true'
      - 'false'
    Description: >-
      Indicates whether the template approval workflow is enabled
      ("true" or "false").

Resources:

  # Signaling endpoint for the template approval workflow. No DependsOn is
  # required between this resource and the SSM parameter below: they are
  # independent of one another and their only implicit dependencies are on the
  # template parameters.
  ApprovalWorkflowSignal:
    Type: AWS::CloudFormation::WaitConditionHandle
    Metadata:
      Purpose: Template approval workflow validation signaling endpoint
      Greeting: !Sub "Hello, ${Name}! This is a test resource for validating the template approval workflow."
      CustomMessage: !Ref CustomMessage
      # CloudFormation exposes no timestamp pseudo parameter, so the timestamp
      # value is composed dynamically from the Name parameter and stack pseudo
      # parameters. No literal timestamps, region names, or account IDs are
      # hardcoded.
      Timestamp: !Sub "${AWS::StackName}-${Name}-${AWS::StackId}"

  # Transient test resource: DeletionPolicy/UpdateReplacePolicy are
  # intentionally omitted because this parameter is disposable and has no
  # stated data-retention requirement.
  ApprovalWorkflowParameter:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Parameter
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '/iidy/template-approval/test/${Name}'
      Type: String
      Description: Test parameter for template approval workflow validation
      Value: !Sub |
        {
          "stackName": "${AWS::StackName}",
          "stackId": "${AWS::StackId}",
          "customMessage": "${CustomMessage}",
          "approvalWorkflowEnabled": ${ApprovalWorkflowEnabled},
          "region": "${AWS::Region}",
          "accountId": "${AWS::AccountId}"
        }
      Tags:
        Project: TemplateApprovalWorkflow
        Environment: Test
        Purpose: TemplateApprovalWorkflowValidation

Outputs:

  ParameterName:
    Description: >-
      Name (full path) of the SSM parameter created for approval workflow
      validation.
    Value: !Ref ApprovalWorkflowParameter

  Greeting:
    Description: Human-readable greeting for the approval workflow consumer.
    Value: !Sub "Hello, ${Name}! ${CustomMessage}"

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: Provisions a DynamoDB-backed Step Functions standard workflow for testing PutItem and GetItem.

Parameters:
  TableName:
    Type: String
    Default: my-table
    Description: Name of the DynamoDB table used by the Step Functions workflow.

Resources:
  Table:
    Type: AWS::DynamoDB::Table
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      TableName: !Ref TableName
      BillingMode: PAY_PER_REQUEST
      AttributeDefinitions:
        - AttributeName: id
          AttributeType: S
      KeySchema:
        - AttributeName: id
          KeyType: HASH

  StateMachineRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: states.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: DynamoDBAccess
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - dynamodb:PutItem
                  - dynamodb:GetItem
                Resource: !GetAtt Table.Arn

  StateMachine:
    Type: AWS::StepFunctions::StateMachine
    Properties:
      StateMachineType: STANDARD
      RoleArn: !GetAtt StateMachineRole.Arn
      DefinitionString: !Sub |
        {
          "Comment": "DynamoDB-backed testing workflow",
          "StartAt": "PutItem",
          "States": {
            "PutItem": {
              "Type": "Task",
              "Resource": "arn:aws:states:::dynamodb:putItem",
              "Parameters": {
                "TableName": "${Table.Arn}",
                "Item": {
                  "id": {
                    "S.$": "$.id"
                  },
                  "description": {
                    "S.$": "States.Format('Item {} description', $.id)"
                  }
                }
              },
              "ResultPath": null,
              "Next": "GetItem"
            },
            "GetItem": {
              "Type": "Task",
              "Resource": "arn:aws:states:::dynamodb:getItem",
              "Parameters": {
                "TableName": "${Table.Arn}",
                "Key": {
                  "id": {
                    "S.$": "$.id"
                  }
                },
                "ConsistentRead": true
              },
              "ResultSelector": {
                "Item.$": "$.Item"
              },
              "OutputPath": "$.Item",
              "End": true
            }
          }
        }

Outputs:
  StateMachineArn:
    Description: ARN of the Step Functions state machine.
    Value: !GetAtt StateMachine.Arn
  StateMachineName:
    Description: Name of the Step Functions state machine.
    Value: !GetAtt StateMachine.Name
  DynamoDBTableName:
    Description: Name of the DynamoDB table.
    Value: !Ref Table

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: >-
  DevOps Agent Space supporting IAM resources. Creates the agent service role and the
  operator application role, each trusting the AWS DevOps Agent service principal
  (aidevops.amazonaws.com) with aws:SourceAccount and aws:SourceArn conditions, attaches
  AWS managed policies, and grants the agent role least-privilege service-linked-role
  creation. The AWS::DevOpsAgent::AgentSpace resource type could not be confirmed as
  published in the us-east-1 CloudFormation registry, so the agent space resource and its
  primary monitoring account association are intentionally NOT emitted (see the GAP
  comments in Resources) rather than inventing a resource type that would fail at parse
  time. The template remains syntactically valid and deployable.

Parameters:

  AgentSpaceName:
    Type: String
    Default: devops-agent-space
    MinLength: 1
    MaxLength: 48
    AllowedPattern: '^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9-]*$'
    ConstraintDescription: >-
      Must start with an alphanumeric character and contain only alphanumeric
      characters and hyphens.
    Description: >-
      Logical name of the DevOps agent space; used to derive all resource names and the
      source ARN condition scope.

  Environment:
    Type: String
    Default: dev
    AllowedValues:
      - dev
      - test
      - staging
      - prod
    Description: Deployment environment applied as a resource tag.

Resources:

  # ============================================================================
  # GAP: AWS::DevOpsAgent::AgentSpace (and its primary monitoring account
  # association) are intentionally NOT emitted below. The CloudFormation resource
  # type for the DevOps Agent Space could not be confirmed as published in the
  # us-east-1 CloudFormation registry, and a hallucinated type name fails at
  # parse time. When the type is confirmed, add the stateful resource here
  # (DeletionPolicy/UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain), populate the monitoring account
  # association with !Ref 'AWS::AccountId', and wire the SourceArn conditions and
  # the AgentSpaceId / AgentSpaceArn / OperatorUrl outputs to it:
  #
  #   DevOpsAgentSpace:
  #     Type: AWS::DevOpsAgent::AgentSpace          # <-- UNCONFIRMED, DO NOT EMIT
  #     DeletionPolicy: Retain
  #     UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
  #     Properties:
  #       Name: !Ref AgentSpaceName
  #       AgentRoleArn: !GetAtt AgentRole.Arn
  #       OperatorRoleArn: !GetAtt OperatorRole.Arn
  #
  #   DevOpsAgentMonitoringAccountAssociation:      # <-- UNCONFIRMED, DO NOT EMIT
  #     Type: AWS::DevOpsAgent::AgentSpaceAccountAssociation
  #     DependsOn: DevOpsAgentSpace
  #     Properties:
  #       AgentSpaceId: !Ref DevOpsAgentSpace
  #       AccountId: !Ref 'AWS::AccountId'
  # ============================================================================

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Agent service role assumed by the AWS DevOps Agent itself.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  AgentRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: !Sub '${AgentSpaceName}-agent-role'
      Description: !Sub 'Service role assumed by the AWS DevOps Agent for agent space ${AgentSpaceName}.'
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: AllowDevOpsAgentServiceAssumeRole
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: aidevops.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                aws:SourceAccount: !Ref 'AWS::AccountId'
                aws:SourceArn: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:aidevops:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:agent-space/${AgentSpaceName}'
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        # Account-agnostic AWS managed policy (read access required for agent
        # investigation/monitoring). Tighten to the service's documented policy set
        # once published.
        - arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/ReadOnlyAccess
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: AllowCreateDevOpsAgentServiceLinkedRole
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Sid: CreateDevOpsAgentServiceLinkedRole
                Effect: Allow
                Action: iam:CreateServiceLinkedRole
                Resource: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::${AWS::AccountId}:role/aws-service-role/*'
                Condition:
                  StringEquals:
                    iam:AWSServiceName: aidevops.amazonaws.com
      Tags:
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref Environment
        - Key: Component
          Value: DevOpsAgent
        - Key: AgentSpace
          Value: !Ref AgentSpaceName
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: CloudFormation

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Operator application role used by the DevOps Agent operator experience.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  OperatorRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: !Sub '${AgentSpaceName}-operator-role'
      Description: !Sub 'Operator application role for the AWS DevOps Agent agent space ${AgentSpaceName}.'
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: AllowDevOpsAgentServiceAssumeRole
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: aidevops.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                aws:SourceAccount: !Ref 'AWS::AccountId'
                aws:SourceArn: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:aidevops:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:agent-space/${AgentSpaceName}'
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        # Account-agnostic AWS managed policy for the operator experience. Tighten to
        # the service's documented policy set once published.
        - arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/ReadOnlyAccess
      Tags:
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref Environment
        - Key: Component
          Value: DevOpsAgent
        - Key: AgentSpace
          Value: !Ref AgentSpaceName
        - Key: ManagedBy
          Value: CloudFormation

Outputs:

  AgentSpaceName:
    Description: Name of the DevOps agent space.
    Value: !Ref AgentSpaceName

  AgentRoleArn:
    Description: ARN of the DevOps agent service role.
    Value: !GetAtt AgentRole.Arn

  OperatorRoleArn:
    Description: ARN of the DevOps agent operator application role.
    Value: !GetAtt OperatorRole.Arn

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # The following outputs require the (unconfirmed) AWS::DevOpsAgent::AgentSpace
  # resource and are intentionally omitted until the type is confirmed:
  #   AgentSpaceId   -> !Ref  DevOpsAgentSpace
  #   AgentSpaceArn  -> !GetAtt DevOpsAgentSpace.Arn
  #   OperatorUrl    -> !GetAtt DevOpsAgentSpace.OperatorUrl (confirm the attribute

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: >-
  Lambda-based CI/CD deployment environment. Creates a main Lambda function with a
  published version and a "live" alias, pre-traffic and post-traffic validation hook
  functions, the supporting IAM roles, a customer-managed KMS key and an artifacts S3
  bucket for the CodeDeploy AppSpec revision, and an AWS CodeDeploy application and
  deployment group configured for blue/green canary traffic shifting with automatic
  rollback.

Parameters:
  EnvironmentName:
    Type: String
    Default: dev
    AllowedValues:
      - dev
      - staging
      - prod
    Description: Application environment name used for tagging and for the main Lambda function configuration.

Resources:

  #############################################################################
  # Customer-managed KMS key that encrypts the CodeDeploy AppSpec artifacts.
  # The account-root statement enables IAM identity policies in this account
  # (notably the CodeDeploy service role's inline decrypt policy) to grant
  # access to the key, which keeps the dependency graph one-way and acyclic.
  #############################################################################
  ArtifactsKey:
    Type: AWS::KMS::Key
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      Description: Customer-managed key used to encrypt CodeDeploy AppSpec artifacts.
      EnableKeyRotation: true
      PendingWindowInDays: 30
      KeyPolicy:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: AllowAccountRootFullKeyAdministration
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              AWS: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::${AWS::AccountId}:root'
            Action: 'kms:*'
            Resource: '*'
      Tags:
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref EnvironmentName

  #############################################################################
  # S3 bucket that stores the CodeDeploy Lambda AppSpec revision. The revision
  # is uploaded by the CI/CD pipeline at deploy time via s3:PutObject; that
  # writer principal also requires kms:GenerateDataKey and kms:Decrypt on the
  # ArtifactsKey because the bucket now defaults to SSE-KMS.
  #############################################################################
  ArtifactsBucket:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      VersioningConfiguration:
        Status: Enabled
      BucketEncryption:
        ServerSideEncryptionConfiguration:
          - BucketKeyEnabled: true
            ServerSideEncryptionByDefault:
              SSEAlgorithm: aws:kms
              KMSMasterKeyID: !GetAtt ArtifactsKey.Arn
      OwnershipControls:
        Rules:
          - ObjectOwnership: BucketOwnerEnforced
      PublicAccessBlockConfiguration:
        BlockPublicAcls: true
        BlockPublicPolicy: true
        IgnorePublicAcls: true
        RestrictPublicBuckets: true
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-codedeploy-artifacts'
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref EnvironmentName

  ArtifactsBucketPolicy:
    Type: AWS::S3::BucketPolicy
    Properties:
      Bucket: !Ref ArtifactsBucket
      PolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: DenyInsecureTransport
            Effect: Deny
            Principal: '*'
            Action: 's3:*'
            Resource:
              - !GetAtt ArtifactsBucket.Arn
              - !Sub '${ArtifactsBucket.Arn}/*'
            Condition:
              Bool:
                'aws:SecureTransport': 'false'
          - Sid: AllowCodeDeployServiceRoleAccess
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              AWS: !GetAtt CodeDeployServiceRole.Arn
            Action:
              - 's3:GetObject'
              - 's3:GetObjectVersion'
              - 's3:ListBucket'
            Resource:
              - !GetAtt ArtifactsBucket.Arn
              - !Sub '${ArtifactsBucket.Arn}/*'

  #############################################################################
  # CloudWatch log groups for the main function and the validation hooks
  #############################################################################
  MainFunctionLogGroup:
    Type: AWS::Logs::LogGroup
    Properties:
      LogGroupName: !Sub '/aws/lambda/${AWS::StackName}-main-function'
      RetentionInDays: 30

  PreTrafficHookLogGroup:
    Type: AWS::Logs::LogGroup
    Properties:
      LogGroupName: !Sub '/aws/lambda/${AWS::StackName}-pre-traffic-hook'
      RetentionInDays: 30

  PostTrafficHookLogGroup:
    Type: AWS::Logs::LogGroup
    Properties:
      LogGroupName: !Sub '/aws/lambda/${AWS::StackName}-post-traffic-hook'
      RetentionInDays: 30

  #############################################################################
  # IAM execution role for the main Lambda function
  #############################################################################
  MainFunctionExecutionRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-main-function-role'
      Description: Execution role for the main Lambda function.
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: AllowLambdaServiceToAssumeRole
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: lambda.amazonaws.com
            Action: 'sts:AssumeRole'
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - 'arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole'
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: ScopedCloudWatchLogsAccess
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Sid: WriteApplicationLogs
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - 'logs:CreateLogStream'
                  - 'logs:PutLogEvents'
                Resource:
                  - !GetAtt MainFunctionLogGroup.Arn
                  - !Sub '${MainFunctionLogGroup.Arn}:*'
      Tags:
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref EnvironmentName

  #############################################################################
  # IAM execution role shared by the validation hook functions
  #############################################################################
  HookFunctionExecutionRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-hook-function-role'
      Description: Execution role shared by the CodeDeploy validation hook Lambda functions.
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: AllowLambdaServiceToAssumeRole
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: lambda.amazonaws.com
            Action: 'sts:AssumeRole'
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - 'arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole'
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: ReportCodeDeployHookExecutionStatus
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Sid: PutLifecycleEventHookExecutionStatus
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - 'codedeploy:PutLifecycleEventHookExecutionStatus'
                Resource:
                  - !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:codedeploy:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:deploymentgroup:${CodeDeployApplication}/*'
        - PolicyName: ScopedCloudWatchLogsAccess
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Sid: WriteHookLogs
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - 'logs:CreateLogStream'
                  - 'logs:PutLogEvents'
                Resource:
                  - !GetAtt PreTrafficHookLogGroup.Arn
                  - !Sub '${PreTrafficHookLogGroup.Arn}:*'
                  - !GetAtt PostTrafficHookLogGroup.Arn
                  - !Sub '${PostTrafficHookLogGroup.Arn}:*'
      Tags:
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref EnvironmentName

  #############################################################################
  # IAM service role assumed by AWS CodeDeploy
  #############################################################################
  CodeDeployServiceRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-codedeploy-service-role'
      Description: Service role that allows CodeDeploy to manage Lambda alias traffic shifting and read AppSpec artifacts.
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: AllowCodeDeployServiceToAssumeRole
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: codedeploy.amazonaws.com
            Action: 'sts:AssumeRole'
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - 'arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AWSCodeDeployRoleForLambda'
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: DecryptAppSpecArtifacts
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Sid: DecryptAndDescribeArtifactsKey
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - 'kms:Decrypt'
                  - 'kms:DescribeKey'
                Resource:
                  - !GetAtt ArtifactsKey.Arn
      Tags:
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref EnvironmentName

  #############################################################################
  # Main application Lambda function, published version and "live" alias
  #############################################################################
  MyFunction:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    Properties:
      FunctionName: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-main-function'
      Description: Main application function deployed with CodeDeploy blue/green traffic shifting.
      Runtime: python3.12
      Handler: index.handler
      Role: !GetAtt MainFunctionExecutionRole.Arn
      MemorySize: 256
      Timeout: 30
      Environment:
        Variables:
          LOG_LEVEL: INFO
          STAGE: !Ref EnvironmentName
      Code:
        ZipFile: |
          import json
          import logging
          import os

          LOG_LEVEL = os.environ.get("LOG_LEVEL", "INFO")
          STAGE = os.environ.get("STAGE", "dev")

          logger = logging.getLogger()
          logger.setLevel(LOG_LEVEL)


          def handler(event, context):
              logger.info("Received event: %s", json.dumps(event, default=str))
              return {
                  "statusCode": 200,
                  "body": json.dumps(
                      {
                          "message": "Hello from the main Lambda function",
                          "stage": STAGE,
                      }
                  ),
              }
      Tags:
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref EnvironmentName

  MyFunctionVersion:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Version
    Properties:
      FunctionName: !Ref MyFunction
      Description: Initial published version of the main Lambda function.

  MyFunctionAlias:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Alias
    Properties:
      Name: live
      Description: Alias used by AWS CodeDeploy for blue/green traffic shifting.
      FunctionName: !Ref MyFunction
      FunctionVersion: !GetAtt MyFunctionVersion.Version

  #############################################################################
  # Pre-traffic (beforeAllowTraffic) validation hook
  #############################################################################
  PreTrafficHookFunction:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    Properties:
      FunctionName: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-pre-traffic-hook'
      Description: CodeDeploy beforeAllowTraffic validation hook.
      Runtime: python3.12
      Handler: index.handler
      Role: !GetAtt HookFunctionExecutionRole.Arn
      MemorySize: 128
      Timeout: 60
      Environment:
        Variables:
          LOG_LEVEL: INFO
          STAGE: !Ref EnvironmentName
      Code:
        ZipFile: |
          import json
          import logging
          import os

          import boto3

          logger = logging.getLogger()
          logger.setLevel(os.environ.get("LOG_LEVEL", "INFO"))

          codedeploy = boto3.client("codedeploy")


          def handler(event, context):
              logger.info("Pre-traffic hook event: %s", json.dumps(event, default=str))

              deployment_id = event["DeploymentId"]
              hook_execution_id = event["LifecycleEventHookExecutionId"]

              status = "Succeeded"
              try:
                  # Add pre-traffic validation logic here (smoke tests, synthetic
                  # checks, dependency verification, and so on).
                  logger.info("Pre-traffic validation passed for deployment %s", deployment_id)
              except Exception as error:
                  logger.exception("Pre-traffic validation failed for deployment %s: %s", deployment_id, error)
                  status = "Failed"

              codedeploy.put_lifecycle_event_hook_execution_status(
                  deploymentId=deployment_id,
                  lifecycleEventHookExecutionId=hook_execution_id,
                  status=status,
              )

              return {"status": status}
      Tags:
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref EnvironmentName

  PreTrafficHookVersion:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Version
    Properties:
      FunctionName: !Ref PreTrafficHookFunction
      Description: Published version of the pre-traffic validation hook.

  #############################################################################
  # Post-traffic (afterAllowTraffic) validation hook
  #############################################################################
  PostTrafficHookFunction:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    Properties:
      FunctionName: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-post-traffic-hook'
      Description: CodeDeploy afterAllowTraffic validation hook.
      Runtime: python3.12
      Handler: index.handler
      Role: !GetAtt HookFunctionExecutionRole.Arn
      MemorySize: 128
      Timeout: 60
      Environment:
        Variables:
          LOG_LEVEL: INFO
          STAGE: !Ref EnvironmentName
      Code:
        ZipFile: |
          import json
          import logging
          import os

          import boto3

          logger = logging.getLogger()
          logger.setLevel(os.environ.get("LOG_LEVEL", "INFO"))

          codedeploy = boto3.client("codedeploy")


          def handler(event, context):
              logger.info("Post-traffic hook event: %s", json.dumps(event, default=str))

              deployment_id = event["DeploymentId"]
              hook_execution_id = event["LifecycleEventHookExecutionId"]

              status = "Succeeded"
              try:
                  # Add post-traffic validation logic here (functional tests against
                  # the newly shifted traffic, error-rate checks, and so on).
                  logger.info("Post-traffic validation passed for deployment %s", deployment_id)
              except Exception as error:
                  logger.exception("Post-traffic validation failed for deployment %s: %s", deployment_id, error)
                  status = "Failed"

              codedeploy.put_lifecycle_event_hook_execution_status(
                  deploymentId=deployment_id,
                  lifecycleEventHookExecutionId=hook_execution_id,
                  status=status,
              )

              return {"status": status}
      Tags:
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref EnvironmentName

  PostTrafficHookVersion:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Version
    Properties:
      FunctionName: !Ref PostTrafficHookFunction
      Description: Published version of the post-traffic validation hook.

  #############################################################################
  # Allow CodeDeploy (application in this stack) to invoke the main function
  #############################################################################
  MainFunctionInvokePermission:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Permission
    Properties:
      Action: 'lambda:InvokeFunction'
      FunctionName: !Ref MyFunction
      Principal: 'codedeploy.amazonaws.com'
      SourceAccount: !Ref 'AWS::AccountId'
      SourceArn: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:codedeploy:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:application:${CodeDeployApplication}'

  #############################################################################
  # Alarm used by CodeDeploy to detect a bad deployment
  #############################################################################
  MainFunctionErrorAlarm:
    Type: AWS::CloudWatch::Alarm
    Properties:
      AlarmName: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-main-function-errors'
      AlarmDescription: Triggers a CodeDeploy rollback when the main Lambda function reports errors.
      Namespace: AWS/Lambda
      MetricName: Errors
      Statistic: Sum
      Period: 60
      EvaluationPeriods: 1
      Threshold: 1
      ComparisonOperator: GreaterThanOrEqualToThreshold
      TreatMissingData: notBreaching
      Dimensions:
        - Name: FunctionName
          Value: !Ref MyFunction

  #############################################################################
  # CodeDeploy application and blue/green deployment group
  #############################################################################
  CodeDeployApplication:
    Type: AWS::CodeDeploy::Application
    Properties:
      ApplicationName: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-lambda-app'
      ComputePlatform: Lambda
      Tags:
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref EnvironmentName

  CodeDeployDeploymentGroup:
    Type: AWS::CodeDeploy::DeploymentGroup
    Properties:
      ApplicationName: !Ref CodeDeployApplication
      DeploymentGroupName: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-lambda-deployment-group'
      ServiceRoleArn: !GetAtt CodeDeployServiceRole.Arn
      DeploymentConfigName: CodeDeployDefault.LambdaCanary10Percent5Minutes
      DeploymentStyle:
        DeploymentOption: WITH_TRAFFIC_CONTROL
        DeploymentType: BLUE_GREEN
      AlarmConfiguration:
        Enabled: true
        Alarms:
          - Name: !Ref MainFunctionErrorAlarm
      AutoRollbackConfiguration:
        Enabled: true
        Events:
          - DEPLOYMENT_FAILURE
          - DEPLOYMENT_STOP_ON_ALARM
      Tags:
        - Key: Environment
          Value: !Ref EnvironmentName

Outputs:

    Description: Name of the main Lambda function.
    Value: !Ref MyFunction

  MainFunctionArn:
    Description: ARN of the main Lambda function.
    Value: !GetAtt MyFunction.Arn

  MainFunctionAliasArn:
    Description: ARN of the "live" alias used by CodeDeploy for traffic shifting.
    Value: !Sub '${MyFunction.Arn}:live'

  MainFunctionVersion:
    Description: Published version of the main Lambda function.
    Value: !GetAtt MyFunctionVersion.Version

  PreTrafficHookFunctionName:
    Description: Name of the beforeAllowTraffic validation hook function, used as hooks.BeforeAllowTraffic in the AppSpec revision.
    Value: !Ref PreTrafficHookFunction

  PreTrafficHookVersionArn:
    Description: Version-qualified ARN of the beforeAllowTraffic validation hook.
    Value: !Sub '${PreTrafficHookFunction.Arn}:${PreTrafficHookVersion.Version}'

  PostTrafficHookFunctionName:
    Description: Name of the afterAllowTraffic validation hook function, used as hooks.AfterAllowTraffic in the AppSpec revision.
    Value: !Ref PostTrafficHookFunction

  PostTrafficHookVersionArn:
    Description: Version-qualified ARN of the afterAllowTraffic validation hook.

  CodeDeployApplicationName:

  ArtifactsKeyArn:
    Description: ARN of the customer-managed KMS key that encrypts the AppSpec artifacts. The pipeline writer requires kms:GenerateDataKey and kms:Decrypt on this key.
    Value: !GetAtt ArtifactsKey.Arn

  AppSpecKey:
    Description: Conventional S3 key the CI/CD pipeline is expected to write the AppSpec revision to; the stack does not create this object.
    Value: 'appspec/appspec.json'

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: >-
  Pet shop GraphQL API using AWS AppSync for testing purposes. Provisions a
  PetShopAPI with API_KEY authentication for anonymous access, a Lambda
  function that returns a static list of pets (Buddy, Mittens, Charlie), an
  AWS_LAMBDA data source, and a getPets query resolved by that data source.

Resources:

  PetShopLambdaRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: lambda.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole

  PetShopFunction:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    Properties:
      Description: Returns a static list of pets for the PetShopAPI getPets query.
      Runtime: python3.12
      Handler: index.handler
      Role: !GetAtt PetShopLambdaRole.Arn
      Timeout: 15
      MemorySize: 128
      Code:
        ZipFile: |
          import json


          def handler(event, context):
              pets = [
                  {"id": "1", "name": "Buddy", "type": "dog"},
                  {"id": "2", "name": "Mittens", "type": "cat"},
                  {"id": "3", "name": "Charlie", "type": "dog"},
              ]
              return pets

  PetShopAppSyncRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: appsync.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: InvokePetShopFunction
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - lambda:InvokeFunction
                Resource:
                  - !GetAtt PetShopFunction.Arn

  PetShopAPI:
    Type: AWS::AppSync::GraphQLApi
    Properties:
      Name: PetShopAPI
      AuthenticationType: API_KEY

  PetShopApiKey:
    Type: AWS::AppSync::ApiKey
    Properties:
      ApiId: !GetAtt PetShopAPI.ApiId
      Description: API key enabling anonymous access to the PetShopAPI
      Expires: 1798761600

  PetShopSchema:
    Type: AWS::AppSync::GraphQLSchema
    Properties:
      ApiId: !GetAtt PetShopAPI.ApiId
      Definition: |
        type Pet {
          id: ID!
          name: String!
          type: String!
        }

        type Query {
          getPets: [Pet]
        }

  PetShopDataSource:
    Type: AWS::AppSync::DataSource
    Properties:
      ApiId: !GetAtt PetShopAPI.ApiId
      Name: PetShopLambdaDataSource
      Description: Lambda data source backing the getPets query.
      Type: AWS_LAMBDA
      ServiceRoleArn: !GetAtt PetShopAppSyncRole.Arn
      LambdaConfig:
        LambdaFunctionArn: !GetAtt PetShopFunction.Arn

  GetPetsResolver:
    Type: AWS::AppSync::Resolver
    DependsOn: PetShopSchema
    Properties:
      ApiId: !GetAtt PetShopAPI.ApiId
      TypeName: Query
      FieldName: getPets
      DataSourceName: !GetAtt PetShopDataSource.Name
      Kind: UNIT
      RequestMappingTemplate: |
        {
          "version": "2018-05-29",
          "operation": "Invoke",
          "payload": $util.toJson($context)

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: >-
  Provisions the PCI compliance remediation prerequisites used by AWS Config
  Conformance Pack remediations: the pciautomationassumerole<region> IAM role
  that trusts AWS Systems Manager, Amazon EC2 and Amazon EventBridge, plus the
  four custom AWS Systems Manager Automation documents that restrict the VPC
  default security group, delete unused security groups, release unassociated
  Elastic IP addresses, and update an Auto Scaling group health check type to
  ELB with a 300 second grace period.

Parameters:
  DefaultSecurityGroupName:
    Type: String
    Default: default
    MinLength: 1
    MaxLength: 255
    Description: >-
      Name of the security group that AWS creates automatically in every VPC and
      whose ingress and egress rules are revoked by the
      PCIAutomation-RevokeDefaultSecurityGroupRules automation document. It is
      also excluded from deletion by the
      PCIAutomation-DeleteUnusedSecurityGroups automation document.

Resources:

  # Prerequisite role that every remediation automation document assumes.
  PciAutomationAssumeRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: !Sub 'pciautomationassumerole${AWS::Region}'
      Description: >-
        Prerequisite IAM role assumed by the PCI compliance Systems Manager
        Automation documents that are invoked by AWS Config Conformance Pack
        remediation actions.
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: AllowPciAutomationServicesToAssumeRole
            Effect: Allow
            Action: 'sts:AssumeRole'
            Principal:
              Service:
                - ssm.amazonaws.com
                - ec2.amazonaws.com
                - events.amazonaws.com
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: PCIAutomationRemediationPolicy
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              # Least privilege: only the EC2 actions the remediation scripts
              # invoke. None of these EC2 actions support resource level
              # permissions, so Resource must remain '*'.
              - Sid: EC2RemediationActions
                Effect: Allow
                Resource: '*'
                Action:
                  - ec2:ReleaseAddress
                  - ec2:DescribeAddresses
                  - ec2:DescribeSecurityGroups
                  - ec2:DeleteSecurityGroup
                  - ec2:RevokeSecurityGroupIngress
                  - ec2:RevokeSecurityGroupEgress
              # PCIAutomation-UpdateAutoScalingGroupHealthCheck calls the Auto
              # Scaling APIs, which are not EC2 actions and are therefore
              # outside the EC2 action set. They are granted here so that the
              # document can actually run instead of failing at execution time.
              - Sid: AutoScalingRemediationActions
                Effect: Allow
                Resource: '*'
                Action:
                  - autoscaling:DescribeAutoScalingGroups
                  - autoscaling:UpdateAutoScalingGroup
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Sub 'pciautomationassumerole${AWS::Region}'
        - Key: Purpose
          Value: PCIComplianceRemediation

  # 1. Revoke all ingress and egress rules from the VPC default security group.
  RevokeDefaultSecurityGroupRulesDocument:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Document
    Properties:
      Name: PCIAutomation-RevokeDefaultSecurityGroupRules
      DocumentType: Automation
      Content:
        schemaVersion: '0.3'
        description: >-
          Revokes all ingress and egress rules from the default security group
          of the specified VPC.
        assumeRole: '{{ AutomationAssumeRole }}'
        parameters:
          VpcId:
            type: String
            description: >-
              (Required) The ID of the VPC whose default security group rules
              are revoked.
          AutomationAssumeRole:
            type: String
            description: >-
              (Optional) The ARN of the IAM role that allows Automation to
              perform the actions on your behalf.
            default: !GetAtt PciAutomationAssumeRole.Arn
        mainSteps:
          - name: DescribeDefaultSecurityGroup
            action: aws:executeAwsApi
            inputs:
              Service: ec2
              Api: DescribeSecurityGroups
              Filters:
                - Name: vpc-id
                  Values:
                    - '{{ VpcId }}'
                - Name: group-name
                  Values:
                    - !Ref DefaultSecurityGroupName
            outputs:
              - Name: GroupId
                Selector: '$.SecurityGroups[0].GroupId'
                Type: String
          - name: RevokeDefaultSecurityGroupRules
            action: aws:executeScript
            isEnd: true
            inputs:
              Runtime: python3.11
              Handler: revoke_default_group_rules
              InputPayload:
                GroupId: '{{ DescribeDefaultSecurityGroup.GroupId }}'
              Script: |-
                import boto3

                def revoke_default_group_rules(events, context):
                    ec2 = boto3.client('ec2')
                    group_id = events['GroupId']
                    group = ec2.describe_security_groups(GroupIds=[group_id]).get('SecurityGroups', [])[0]
                    ingress_rules = group.get('IpPermissions', [])
                    egress_rules = group.get('IpPermissionsEgress', [])
                    if ingress_rules:
                        ec2.revoke_security_group_ingress(GroupId=group_id, IpPermissions=ingress_rules)
                    if egress_rules:
                        ec2.revoke_security_group_egress(GroupId=group_id, IpPermissions=egress_rules)
                    return {
                        'GroupId': group_id,
                        'RevokedIngressRuleCount': len(ingress_rules),
                        'RevokedEgressRuleCount': len(egress_rules)
                    }

  # 2. Delete security groups that are not attached to any network interface.
  DeleteUnusedSecurityGroupsDocument:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Document
    Properties:
      Name: PCIAutomation-DeleteUnusedSecurityGroups
      DocumentType: Automation
      Content:
        schemaVersion: '0.3'
        description: >-
          Deletes the specified security groups when they are not associated
          with any network interface.
        assumeRole: '{{ AutomationAssumeRole }}'
        parameters:
          SecurityGroupIds:
            type: String
            description: >-
              (Required) Comma separated list of security group IDs to evaluate
              and delete when they are not in use.
          AutomationAssumeRole:
            type: String
            description: >-
              (Optional) The ARN of the IAM role that allows Automation to
              perform the actions on your behalf.
            default: !GetAtt PciAutomationAssumeRole.Arn
        mainSteps:
          - name: DeleteUnusedSecurityGroups
            action: aws:executeScript
            isEnd: true
            inputs:
              Runtime: python3.11
              Handler: delete_unused_security_groups
              InputPayload:
                SecurityGroupIds: '{{ SecurityGroupIds }}'
                DefaultSecurityGroupName: !Ref DefaultSecurityGroupName
              Script: |-
                import boto3

                def delete_unused_security_groups(events, context):
                    ec2 = boto3.client('ec2')
                    default_group_name = events['DefaultSecurityGroupName']
                    group_ids = [value.strip() for value in events['SecurityGroupIds'].split(',') if value.strip()]
                    deleted = []
                    skipped = []
                    for group_id in group_ids:
                        try:
                            groups = ec2.describe_security_groups(GroupIds=[group_id]).get('SecurityGroups', [])
                        except Exception as error:
                            skipped.append({'GroupId': group_id, 'Reason': str(error)})
                            continue
                        if not groups:
                            skipped.append({'GroupId': group_id, 'Reason': 'Security group not found.'})
                            continue
                        group = groups[0]
                        if group.get('GroupName') == default_group_name:
                            skipped.append({'GroupId': group_id, 'Reason': 'The default security group cannot be deleted.'})
                            continue
                        if group.get('NetworkInterfaces'):
                            skipped.append({'GroupId': group_id, 'Reason': 'The security group is associated with one or more network interfaces.'})
                            continue
                        try:
                            ec2.delete_security_group(GroupId=group_id)
                        except Exception as error:
                            skipped.append({'GroupId': group_id, 'Reason': str(error)})
                            continue
                        deleted.append(group_id)
                    return {'DeletedSecurityGroups': deleted, 'SkippedSecurityGroups': skipped}

  # 3. Release unassociated Elastic IP addresses by allocation ID.
  ReleaseUnassociatedElasticIpsDocument:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Document
    Properties:
      Name: PCIAutomation-ReleaseUnassociatedElasticIps
      DocumentType: Automation
      Content:
        schemaVersion: '0.3'
        description: >-
          Releases the specified unassociated Elastic IP addresses.
        assumeRole: '{{ AutomationAssumeRole }}'
        parameters:
          AllocationIds:
            type: String
            description: >-
              (Required) Comma separated list of Elastic IP address allocation
              IDs to release.
          AutomationAssumeRole:
            type: String
            description: >-
              (Optional) The ARN of the IAM role that allows Automation to
              perform the actions on your behalf.
            default: !GetAtt PciAutomationAssumeRole.Arn
        mainSteps:
          - name: ReleaseUnassociatedAddresses
            action: aws:executeScript
            isEnd: true
            inputs:
              Runtime: python3.11
              Handler: release_unassociated_addresses
              InputPayload:
                AllocationIds: '{{ AllocationIds }}'
              Script: |-
                import boto3

                def release_unassociated_addresses(events, context):
                    ec2 = boto3.client('ec2')
                    allocation_ids = [value.strip() for value in events['AllocationIds'].split(',') if value.strip()]
                    released = []
                    skipped = []
                    for allocation_id in allocation_ids:
                        try:
                            addresses = ec2.describe_addresses(AllocationIds=[allocation_id]).get('Addresses', [])
                        except Exception as error:
                            skipped.append({'AllocationId': allocation_id, 'Reason': str(error)})
                            continue
                        if not addresses:
                            skipped.append({'AllocationId': allocation_id, 'Reason': 'Elastic IP address not found.'})
                            continue
                        address = addresses[0]
                        if address.get('AssociationId') or address.get('InstanceId') or address.get('NetworkInterfaceId'):
                            skipped.append({'AllocationId': allocation_id, 'Reason': 'The Elastic IP address is associated with a resource.'})
                            continue
                        try:
                            ec2.release_address(AllocationId=allocation_id)
                        except Exception as error:
                            skipped.append({'AllocationId': allocation_id, 'Reason': str(error)})
                            continue
                        released.append(allocation_id)
                    return {'ReleasedAddresses': released, 'SkippedAddresses': skipped}

  # 4. Set the Auto Scaling group health check type to ELB with a 300 second grace period.
  UpdateAutoScalingGroupHealthCheckDocument:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Document
    Properties:
      Name: PCIAutomation-UpdateAutoScalingGroupHealthCheck
      DocumentType: Automation
      Content:
        schemaVersion: '0.3'
        description: >-
          Updates an Auto Scaling group to use ELB health checks with a health
          check grace period of 300 seconds.
        assumeRole: '{{ AutomationAssumeRole }}'
        parameters:
          AutoScalingGroupName:
            type: String
            description: >-
              (Required) The name of the Auto Scaling group to update.
          AutomationAssumeRole:
            type: String
            description: >-
              (Optional) The ARN of the IAM role that allows Automation to
              perform the actions on your behalf.
            default: !GetAtt PciAutomationAssumeRole.Arn
        mainSteps:
          - name: DescribeAutoScalingGroup
            action: aws:executeAwsApi
            inputs:
              Service: autoscaling
              Api: DescribeAutoScalingGroups
              AutoScalingGroupNames:
                - '{{ AutoScalingGroupName }}'
            outputs:
              - Name: CurrentHealthCheckType
                Selector: '$.AutoScalingGroups[0].HealthCheckType'
                Type: String
          - name: UpdateAutoScalingGroupHealthCheck
            action: aws:executeAwsApi
            isEnd: true
            inputs:
              Service: autoscaling
              Api: UpdateAutoScalingGroup
              AutoScalingGroupName: '{{ AutoScalingGroupName }}'
              HealthCheckType: ELB
              HealthCheckGracePeriod: 300

Outputs:
  PCIAutomationAssumeRoleName:
    Description: Name of the prerequisite automation role.
    Value: !Ref PciAutomationAssumeRole
  PCIAutomationAssumeRoleArn:
    Description: ARN of the prerequisite automation role.
    Value: !GetAtt PciAutomationAssumeRole.Arn
  RevokeDefaultSecurityGroupRulesDocumentName:
    Description: Name of the automation document that revokes VPC default security group rules.
    Value: !Ref RevokeDefaultSecurityGroupRulesDocument
  # AWS::SSM::Document exposes only Ref (the document name) and documents no
  # Fn::GetAtt attributes, so the document ARN is composed with Fn::Sub from
  # this template's own document and the partition, region and account pseudo
  # parameters.
  RevokeDefaultSecurityGroupRulesDocumentArn:
    Description: ARN of the automation document that revokes VPC default security group rules.
    Value: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:ssm:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:document/${RevokeDefaultSecurityGroupRulesDocument}'
  DeleteUnusedSecurityGroupsDocumentName:
    Description: Name of the automation document that deletes unused security groups.
    Value: !Ref DeleteUnusedSecurityGroupsDocument
  DeleteUnusedSecurityGroupsDocumentArn:
    Description: ARN of the automation document that deletes unused security groups.
    Value: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:ssm:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:document/${DeleteUnusedSecurityGroupsDocument}'
  ReleaseUnassociatedElasticIpsDocumentName:
    Description: Name of the automation document that releases unassociated Elastic IP addresses.
    Value: !Ref ReleaseUnassociatedElasticIpsDocument
  ReleaseUnassociatedElasticIpsDocumentArn:
    Description: ARN of the automation document that releases unassociated Elastic IP addresses.
    Value: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:ssm:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:document/${ReleaseUnassociatedElasticIpsDocument}'
  UpdateAutoScalingGroupHealthCheckDocumentName:
    Description: Name of the automation document that updates an Auto Scaling group health check type.
    Value: !Ref UpdateAutoScalingGroupHealthCheckDocument
  UpdateAutoScalingGroupHealthCheckDocumentArn:
    Description: ARN of the automation document that updates an Auto Scaling group health check type.
    Value: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:ssm:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:document/${UpdateAutoScalingGroupHealthCheckDocument}'

    AllowedPattern: '^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9])?$'
    Description: Host label that carries the Campaign Monitor MX record.

  CampaignMonitorMxTarget:
    Type: String
    Default: 'mx.cmail1.com.'
    MaxLength: 255
    Description: >-
      Fully qualified Campaign Monitor mail exchanger. Leave empty to skip the Campaign Monitor
      MX record.

  GoogleWorkspaceDkimValue:
    Type: String
    Default: ''
    MaxLength: 1024
    Description: >-
      Google Workspace DKIM public key (v=DKIM1; k=rsa; p=...) published at
      google._domainkey. Leave empty to skip the record.

  SupercastDkimSelector:
    Type: String
    Default: supercast
    MinLength: 1
    MaxLength: 63
    AllowedPattern: '^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9])?$'
    Description: Supercast DKIM selector (the label in <selector>._domainkey).

  SupercastDkimValue:
    Type: String
    Default: ''
    MaxLength: 1024
    Description: >-
      Supercast DKIM public key published at <selector>._domainkey. Leave empty to skip the
      record.

  SupercastReturnPathHost:
    Type: String
    Default: rp
    MinLength: 1
    MaxLength: 63
    AllowedPattern: '^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9])?$'
    Description: Host label used for the Supercast return-path CNAME.

  SupercastReturnPathTarget:
    Type: String
    Default: 'return-path.supercast.com.'
    MaxLength: 255
    Description: >-
      Fully qualified Supercast return-path target. Leave empty to skip the return-path CNAME.

Conditions:
  HasGoogleSiteVerification: !Not [!Equals [!Ref GoogleSiteVerificationToken, '']]
  HasZoomVerification: !Not [!Equals [!Ref ZoomVerificationToken, '']]
  HasDmarcRua: !Not [!Equals [!Ref DmarcRuaAddress, '']]
  HasAtProto: !Not [!Equals [!Ref AtProtoDid, '']]
  HasZenDeskVerification: !Not [!Equals [!Ref ZenDeskVerificationToken, '']]
  HasZenDeskSubdomain: !Not [!Equals [!Ref ZenDeskSubdomain, '']]
  HasZenDeskDkim: !Not [!Equals [!Ref ZenDeskDkimValue, '']]
  HasCampaignMonitorDkim: !Not [!Equals [!Ref CampaignMonitorDkimValue, '']]
  HasCampaignMonitorSpf: !Not [!Equals [!Ref CampaignMonitorSpfInclude, '']]
  HasCampaignMonitorMx: !Not [!Equals [!Ref CampaignMonitorMxTarget, '']]
  HasGoogleWorkspaceDkim: !Not [!Equals [!Ref GoogleWorkspaceDkimValue, '']]
  HasSupercastDkim: !Not [!Equals [!Ref SupercastDkimValue, '']]
  HasSupercastReturnPath: !Not [!Equals [!Ref SupercastReturnPathTarget, '']]

Resources:

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Hosted zone (retained on stack delete / replace so delegation survives)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  HostedZone:
    Type: AWS::Route53::HostedZone
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      Name: !Ref DomainName
      HostedZoneConfig:
        Comment: !Sub 'Ear Hustle production DNS zone for ${DomainName}'
      HostedZoneTags:
        - Key: prx:ops:environment
          Value: Production
        - Key: prx:dev:application
          Value: Ear Hustle
        - Key: prx:ops:owner
          Value: prx-ops
        - Key: prx:dev:repo
          Value: ear-hustle-dns

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Apex web records (Squarespace)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  ApexARecord:
    Type: AWS::Route53::RecordSet
    Properties:
      HostedZoneId: !Ref HostedZone
      Name: !Sub '${DomainName}.'
      Type: A
      TTL: '300'
      ResourceRecords: !Ref SquarespaceApexIps

  WwwCnameRecord:
    Type: AWS::Route53::RecordSet
    Properties:
      HostedZoneId: !Ref HostedZone
      Name: !Sub 'www.${DomainName}.'
      Type: CNAME
      TTL: '3600'
      ResourceRecords:
        - !Ref SquarespaceWwwTarget

  SquarespaceVerificationCnameRecord:
    Type: AWS::Route53::RecordSet
    Properties:
      HostedZoneId: !Ref HostedZone
      Name: !Sub '${SquarespaceVerificationHost}.${DomainName}.'
      Type: CNAME
      TTL: '300'
      ResourceRecords:
        - !Ref SquarespaceVerificationTarget

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Apex TXT record: SPF + apex-level verification strings + DMARC.
  # All of these services require their value at the apex, and Route 53 allows
  # only one TXT record set per name, so every apex TXT value is published in
  # this single record set. Optional values are dropped when their parameter is
  # empty.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  ApexTxtRecord:
    Type: AWS::Route53::RecordSet
    Properties:
      HostedZoneId: !Ref HostedZone
      Name: !Sub '${DomainName}.'
      Type: TXT
      TTL: '300'
      ResourceRecords:
        - !Sub '"${SpfRecordValue}"'
        - Fn::If:
            - HasGoogleSiteVerification
            - !Sub '"google-site-verification=${GoogleSiteVerificationToken}"'
            - !Ref 'AWS::NoValue'
        - Fn::If:
            - HasZoomVerification
            - !Sub '"zoom-domain-verification=${ZoomVerificationToken}"'
            - !Ref 'AWS::NoValue'
        - Fn::If:
            - HasZenDeskVerification
            - !Sub '"zendesk-verification=${ZenDeskVerificationToken}"'
            - !Ref 'AWS::NoValue'
        - Fn::If:
            - HasDmarcRua
            - !Sub '"v=DMARC1; p=none; rua=mailto:${DmarcRuaAddress}"'
            - '"v=DMARC1; p=none;"'

  # ATProto domain verification record (did=... published at _atproto).
  AtProtoTxtRecord:
    Type: AWS::Route53::RecordSet
    Condition: HasAtProto
    Properties:
      HostedZoneId: !Ref HostedZone
      Name: !Sub '_atproto.${DomainName}.'
      Type: TXT
      TTL: '300'
      ResourceRecords:
        - !Sub '"did=${AtProtoDid}"'

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Mail records (Google Workspace / G Suite)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  ApexMxRecord:
    Type: AWS::Route53::RecordSet
    Properties:
      HostedZoneId: !Ref HostedZone
      Name: !Sub '${DomainName}.'
      Type: MX
      TTL: '3600'
      ResourceRecords:
        - '1 ASPMX.L.GOOGLE.COM.'
        - '5 ALT1.ASPMX.L.GOOGLE.COM.'
        - '5 ALT2.ASPMX.L.GOOGLE.COM.'
        - '10 ALT3.ASPMX.L.GOOGLE.COM.'
        - '10 ALT4.ASPMX.L.GOOGLE.COM.'

  OldSubdomainMxRecord:
    Type: AWS::Route53::RecordSet
    Properties:
      HostedZoneId: !Ref HostedZone
      Name: !Sub '${OldSubdomainName}.${DomainName}.'
      Type: MX
      TTL: '3600'
      ResourceRecords:
        - '1 ASPMX.L.GOOGLE.COM.'
        - '5 ALT1.ASPMX.L.GOOGLE.COM.'
        - '5 ALT2.ASPMX.L.GOOGLE.COM.'
        - '10 ALT3.ASPMX.L.GOOGLE.COM.'
        - '10 ALT4.ASPMX.L.GOOGLE.COM.'

  GoogleWorkspaceDkimTxtRecord:
    Type: AWS::Route53::RecordSet
    Condition: HasGoogleWorkspaceDkim
    Properties:
      HostedZoneId: !Ref HostedZone
      Name: !Sub 'google._domainkey.${DomainName}.'
      Type: TXT
      TTL: '3600'
      ResourceRecords:
        - !Sub '"${GoogleWorkspaceDkimValue}"'

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Podcast feed records (Supercast hosted feeds)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  FeedsCnameRecord:
    Type: AWS::Route53::RecordSet
    Properties:
      HostedZoneId: !Ref HostedZone
      Name: !Sub 'feeds.${DomainName}.'
      Type: CNAME
      TTL: '300'
      ResourceRecords:
        - !Ref FeedsCnameTarget

  PodcastFeedCnameRecord:
    Type: AWS::Route53::RecordSet
    Properties:
      HostedZoneId: !Ref HostedZone
      Name: !Sub '${PodcastSubdomainName}.${DomainName}.'
      Type: CNAME
      TTL: '300'
      ResourceRecords:
        - !Ref FeedsCnameTarget

  SupercastDkimTxtRecord:
    Type: AWS::Route53::RecordSet
    Condition: HasSupercastDkim
    Properties:
      HostedZoneId: !Ref HostedZone
      Name: !Sub '${SupercastDkimSelector}._domainkey.${DomainName}.'
      Type: TXT
      TTL: '3600'
      ResourceRecords:
        - !Sub '"${SupercastDkimValue}"'

  SupercastReturnPathCnameRecord:
    Type: AWS::Route53::RecordSet
    Condition: HasSupercastReturnPath
    Properties:
      HostedZoneId: !Ref HostedZone
      Name: !Sub '${SupercastReturnPathHost}.${DomainName}.'
      Type: CNAME
      TTL: '300'
      ResourceRecords:
        - !Ref SupercastReturnPathTarget

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # ZenDesk records (domain verification, hosted domain CNAME, DKIM)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  ZenDeskDomainCnameRecord:
    Type: AWS::Route53::RecordSet
    Condition: HasZenDeskSubdomain
    Properties:
      HostedZoneId: !Ref HostedZone
      Name: !Sub '${ZenDeskSubdomain}.${DomainName}.'
      Type: CNAME
      TTL: '300'
      ResourceRecords:
        - !Sub '${ZenDeskSubdomain}.zendesk.com.'

  ZenDeskDkim1CnameRecord:
    Type: AWS::Route53::RecordSet
    Condition: HasZenDeskDkim
    Properties:
      HostedZoneId: !Ref HostedZone
      Name: !Sub 'zendesk1._domainkey.${DomainName}.'
      Type: CNAME
      TTL: '300'
      ResourceRecords:
        - 'zendesk1.domainkey.zendesk.com.'

  ZenDeskDkim2CnameRecord:
    Type: AWS::Route53::RecordSet
    Condition: HasZenDeskDkim
    Properties:
      HostedZoneId: !Ref HostedZone
      Name: !Sub 'zendesk2._domainkey.${DomainName}.'
      Type: CNAME
      TTL: '300'
      ResourceRecords:
        - 'zendesk2.domainkey.zendesk.com.'

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Campaign Monitor records (DKIM, SPF alignment, MX)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  CampaignMonitorDkimCnameRecord:
    Type: AWS::Route53::RecordSet
    Condition: HasCampaignMonitorDkim
    Properties:
      HostedZoneId: !Ref HostedZone
      Name: !Sub '${CampaignMonitorDkimSelector}._domainkey.${DomainName}.'
      Type: CNAME
      TTL: '300'
      ResourceRecords:
        - !Sub '${CampaignMonitorDkimSelector}.${CampaignMonitorDkimDomain}'

  CampaignMonitorSpfTxtRecord:
    Type: AWS::Route53::RecordSet
    Condition: HasCampaignMonitorSpf
    Properties:
      HostedZoneId: !Ref HostedZone
      Name: !Sub '${CampaignMonitorSpfHost}.${DomainName}.'
      Type: TXT
      TTL: '300'
      ResourceRecords:
        - !Sub '"v=spf1 include:${CampaignMonitorSpfInclude} ~all"'

  CampaignMonitorMxRecord:
    Type: AWS::Route53::RecordSet
    Condition: HasCampaignMonitorMx
    Properties:
      HostedZoneId: !Ref HostedZone
      Name: !Sub '${CampaignMonitorMxHost}.${DomainName}.'
      Type: MX
      TTL: '3600'
      ResourceRecords:
        - !Sub '10 ${CampaignMonitorMxTarget}'

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # ACM certificate for the feeds subdomain.
  # ValidationMethod is DNS and DomainValidationOptions binds each requested
  # name to this hosted zone, so ACM creates the validation CNAME records
  # automatically. The validation name/target are generated by ACM when the
  # request is made and therefore cannot be hardcoded here.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  FeedsCertificate:
    Type: AWS::CertificateManager::Certificate
    Properties:
      DomainName: !Sub 'feeds.${DomainName}'
      SubjectAlternativeNames:
        - !Ref DomainName
        - !Sub 'www.${DomainName}'
      ValidationMethod: DNS
      DomainValidationOptions:
        - DomainName: !Sub 'feeds.${DomainName}'
          HostedZoneId: !Ref HostedZone
        - DomainName: !Ref DomainName
          HostedZoneId: !Ref HostedZone
        - DomainName: !Sub 'www.${DomainName}'
          HostedZoneId: !Ref HostedZone
      Tags:
        - Key: prx:ops:environment
          Value: Production
        - Key: prx:dev:application
          Value: Ear Hustle
        - Key: prx:ops:owner
          Value: prx-ops
        - Key: prx:dev:repo
          Value: ear-hustle-dns

Outputs:
  HostedZoneId:
    Description: Route 53 hosted zone ID of the apex domain.
    Value: !Ref HostedZone

  HostedZoneName:
    Description: Apex domain name managed by the hosted zone.
    Value: !Ref DomainName

  HostedZoneNameServers:
    Description: Delegation name servers to configure at the domain registrar.
    Value: !Join
      - ','
      - !GetAtt HostedZone.NameServers

  HostedZoneArn:
    Description: ARN of the hosted zone.
    Value: !Sub 'arn:${AWS::Partition}:route53:::hostedzone/${HostedZone}'

  FeedsCertificateArn:
    Description: ARN of the DNS-validated ACM certificate for the feeds subdomain.
    Value: !Ref FeedsCertificate

  FeedsFqdn:
    Description: Fully qualified feeds subdomain covered by the certificate.
    Value: !Sub 'feeds.${DomainName}'

  DeploymentContext:
    Description: Account and Region in which the DNS stack was deployed.
    Value: !Sub '${AWS::AccountId}/${AWS::Region}'
